follow100Note: Supermicro kept $10.60 of every $100 — far more than usual — because gross margin jumped to 17.5% this quarter. Each row is rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent short of the $10.60 kept as profit.
footerNote: Supermicro guided Q1 FY27 net sales to $14.5B–$15.5B and full-year FY27 net sales to $65B–$72B.

oneTimers: Net income was $1,178M; after $13M of preferred stock dividends, net income attributable to common stockholders was $1,165M — the $1.62 diluted EPS is figured on the attributable number.
The August 11 release called its figures preliminary; the Form 10-K filed August 31, 2026 reported the same full-year totals (net sales $39,063M, net income $2,230M).
otherDetail: Non-operating items were a net $18.5M expense: $22.2M of other income, plus $39.1M of interest income, less $79.8M of interest expense. A separate $1.2M share of loss from an equity investee, net of taxes, is shown as equityM (amounts from thousands).

segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split this quarter. Sales are mostly complete AI server and rack systems built on its Data Center Building Block Solutions; the company said it took in more than $60B of new orders during fiscal 2026 and entered FY27 with record backlog.

sources.label: Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended Jun 30, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Net sales rose to $11.1B from $5.8B a year ago and $10.2B in Q3, driven by AI rack demand and several hundred new enterprise customers added during the year.
takeaways.title: Sales nearly doubled

takeaways.text: Gross margin leapt from 9.9% in Q3 and 9.5% a year ago to 17.5%, which management credited to a richer enterprise customer mix and broader DCBBS adoption — the entire profit story of the quarter.
takeaways.title: Margins jumped

takeaways.text: Supermicro guided FY27 net sales to $65B–$72B (vs $39.1B in FY26), backed by more than $60B of new orders booked in fiscal 2026 and record backlog.
takeaways.title: A huge year guided

verdict: Supermicro's sales nearly doubled to $11.1B and gross margin jumped to 17.5% on a richer enterprise mix, turning the quarter into $1.18B of profit — its most profitable quarter yet.
